input.prompt:
Explore the entire codebase thoroughly. I need to understand:
1. The overall directory structure
2. All source files and their contents
3. All test files and their contents
4. The package.json (dependencies, scripts)
5. How the static site generator currently works (frontmatter parsing, page processing, etc.)
6. Any existing configuration files

Return a comprehensive summary of:
- All files with their paths and key content
- How the CLI works
- How pages are processed
- How frontmatter is parsed
- The test structure and what tests exist
- Any template-related code that may already exist

state.output: Now I have a complete picture. Here is the comprehensive summary: --- ## Comprehensive Codebase Summary ### 1. Overall Directory Structure ``` /tmp/story_3befdab6020a/ ├── .git/ # Git repository metadata ├── .instrument/ │ └── session.jsonl # Instrumentation session log ├── node_modules/ # Installed dependencies ├── src/ │ ├── __tests__/ │ │ ├── cli.test.ts # CLI integration tests │ │ ├── generator.test.ts # Generator unit tests │ │ └── parser.test.ts # Parser unit tests │ ├── cli.ts # CLI entry point (the ssg binary) │ ├── generator.ts # HTML output generation │ ├── index.ts # Public API barrel export │ ├── parser.ts # Markdown + frontmatter parsing │ └── types.ts # TypeScript interfaces ├── jest.config.js # Jest configuration ├── package.json # Project manifest ├── package-lock.json # Lock file └── tsconfig.json # TypeScript configuration ``` There are **5 source files** and **3 test files** in the `src/` directory. There is no `.gitignore` file. There is no `dist/` directory (the project is TypeScript but has not been built yet). There are **no existing template files**. --- ### 2. All Source Files and Their Contents #### `/tmp/story_3befdab6020a/src/types.ts` (12 lines) Defines two TypeScript interfaces: - **`Frontmatter`**: `{ title: string; date: string; tags: string[]; }` - **`Page`**: `{ slug: string; frontmatter: Frontmatter; content: string; html: string; }` The `Page` interface combines the raw markdown `content` with its parsed `html` and the extracted `frontmatter`. The `slug` is derived from the filename (without `.md` extension). --- #### `/tmp/story_3befdab6020a/src/parser.ts` (47 lines) The core markdown parsing module. Key details: - **Imports**: `fs`, `path`, `gray-matter`, `marked`, and the `types`. - **Default frontmatter** (`DEFAULT_FRONTMATTER`): `{ title: '', date: '', tags: [] }` -- used as fallback for missing fields. - **`parseMarkdownFiles(contentDir: string): Page[]`**: 1. Resolves the `contentDir` to an absolute path. 2. Reads directory entries with `fs.readdirSync` (with `withFileTypes: true`). 3. Iterates only over files ending with `.md`. 4. For each `.md` file: - Reads the raw file content. - Uses `gray-matter` to parse frontmatter `data` and markdown `content`. - Normalizes the `date` field: if it's a JavaScript `Date` object, converts to `YYYY-MM-DD`; if a string, uses directly; otherwise falls back to empty string. - Extracts `title` (string, default `''`), `date`, and `tags` (array, default `[]`). - Converts markdown content to HTML using `marked.parse()`. - Derives the `slug` by stripping the `.md` extension from the filename. - Pushes a `Page` object into the results array. 5. **Sorts** pages alphabetically by `frontmatter.title` before returning. --- #### `/tmp/story_3befdab6020a/src/generator.ts` (71 lines) The HTML output generation module. Key details: - **`escapeHtml(text: string): string`**: Escapes `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'` to HTML entities for XSS prevention. - **`renderLayout(title: string, body: string): string`**: Returns a complete HTML5 document with a `` containing charset, viewport meta, and ``, and a `<body>` with the given content. **This is the equivalent of a hardcoded template** -- there are no separate template files. - **`renderPage(page: Page): string`**: Builds the page body with: - `<h1>` with the escaped title - Optional date line (`<p>Date: ...</p>`) -- only if `date` is non-empty - Optional tags line (`<p>Tags: ...</p>`) -- only if `tags` array is non-empty - The page's HTML content (from markdown) - A "Back to index" link: `<a href="index.html">Back to index</a>` - **`renderIndex(pages: Page[]): string`**: Builds an index page with: - `<h1>Site Index</h1>` - An unordered list of links to each page (`<a href="{slug}.html">{title}</a>`) - **`generateSite(pages: Page[], outputDir: string): void`**: 1. Creates the output directory recursively (`fs.mkdirSync` with `recursive: true`). 2. For each page, renders the HTML via `renderPage` and writes it to `{slug}.html`. 3. Renders and writes `index.html` via `renderIndex`. --- #### `/tmp/story_3befdab6020a/src/cli.ts` (38 lines) The CLI entry point (registered as `ssg` in `package.json` `bin`). Key details: - **`parseArgs(args: string[]): CliOptions`**: Parses `--content <dir>` (default `./content`) and `--output <dir>` (default `./dist`) from command-line arguments. - **Main flow**: 1. Gets `process.argv.slice(2)`. 2. If the first argument is not `build`, prints usage and exits with code 1. 3. Parses remaining arguments with `parseArgs`. 4. Calls `parseMarkdownFiles(options.content)` and `generateSite(pages, options.output)`. 5. Prints `"Generated {N} page(s) in {outputDir}"` to stdout. - **Usage**: `ssg build [--content <dir>] [--output <dir>]` --- #### `/tmp/story_3befdab6020a/src/index.ts` (3 lines) Barrel export file -- re-exports `parseMarkdownFiles`, `generateSite`, `Page`, and `Frontmatter` for the public API. --- ### 3. All Test Files and Their Contents #### `/tmp/story_3befdab6020a/src/__tests__/parser.test.ts` (139 lines) Tests for `parseMarkdownFiles`. Uses temp directories created with `fs.mkdtempSync` and cleaned up with `fs.rmSync`. **7 test cases**: 1. **Empty directory** returns `[]`. 2. **No `.md` files** (only `.txt`) returns `[]`. 3. **Single markdown file with full frontmatter** -- verifies slug, title, date, tags, and HTML output (checks for `<h1`, "Hello", "paragraph"). 4. **Multiple markdown files** -- verifies count and alphabetical sorting by title (Alpha before Beta). 5. **Missing frontmatter fields** (only title provided) -- verifies date defaults to `''` and tags to `[]`. 6. **No frontmatter at all** (plain markdown) -- verifies all frontmatter fields get defaults, and HTML still contains `<h1`. 7. **Ignores non-markdown files** (`.txt`, `.png` mixed with `.md`). 8. **Markdown-to-HTML formatting** -- verifies headings, bold, italic, list items, and inline code are converted correctly. #### `/tmp/story_3befdab6020a/src/__tests__/generator.test.ts` (141 lines) Tests for `generateSite`. Has a `makePage` helper factory. Uses temp directories. **11 test cases**: 1. Creates the output directory if it doesn't exist (even nested). 2. Generates `index.html` with correct DOCTYPE, title, and heading. 3. Generates per-page HTML with DOCTYPE, title, heading, and content. 4. Includes date in output when present on frontmatter. 5. Omits date when empty string. 6. Includes tags in output when present. 7. Omits tags section when tags array is empty. 8. Index page links to all pages with correct `href` and anchor text. 9. Pages link back to index (`Back to index`). 10. Valid HTML structure (DOCTYPE, html lang, head, meta charset, body). 11. HTML-escapes special characters in titles (XSS prevention test with `<script>alert`). 12. Generates multiple page files plus index. #### `/tmp/story_3befdab6020a/src/__tests__/cli.test.ts` (127 lines) Integration tests for the CLI. Uses `execSync` with `ts-node` to run the actual CLI. **5 test cases**: 1. **No subcommand** prints usage and exits with code 1. 2. **Default directories** (`./content` and `./dist`) -- creates content, runs `ssg build`, verifies output files exist, then cleans up. 3. **Custom `--content` and `--output` flags** -- verifies files are written to the specified output directory. 4. **Index links all pages** -- creates two markdown files, runs CLI, verifies `index.html` contains links to both. 5. **Empty content directory** -- runs CLI, verifies "Generated 0 page(s)" and that `index.html` still exists. --- ### 4. package.json Details | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | **name** | `ssg` | | **version** | `1.0.0` | | **main** | `dist/index.js` | | **bin** | `{ "ssg": "./dist/cli.js" }` | | **scripts** | `build` (tsc), `test` (jest), `prepack` (npm run build) | **Dependencies** (2): - **`gray-matter` ^4.0.3** -- Frontmatter/YAML parsing from markdown files - **`marked` ^15.0.0** -- Markdown-to-HTML conversion **Dev Dependencies** (5): - `@types/jest` ^29.5.14, `@types/node` ^22.0.0 - `jest` ^29.7.0, `ts-jest` ^29.2.0, `typescript` ^5.7.0 --- ### 5. How the Static Site Generator Works The pipeline is a simple **parse-then-generate** model: ``` Markdown files --> parser.ts --> Page[] --> generator.ts --> HTML files (gray-matter (array of (renderPage, (one .html + marked) Page objects) renderIndex, per page renderLayout) + index.html) ``` **Step-by-step flow:** 1. **CLI** (`cli.ts`) is invoked as `ssg build [--content ./content] [--output ./dist]`. 2. **PARSER** (`parser.ts`) reads all `.md` files from the content directory: - Uses `gray-matter` to split each file into frontmatter (YAML between `---` delimiters) and markdown content. - Uses `marked` to convert markdown content to HTML. - Extracts `title`, `date`, `tags` from frontmatter with defensive defaults. - Sorts pages alphabetically by title. 3. **GENERATOR** (`generator.ts`) takes the array of `Page` objects: - Creates the output directory. - For each page, generates a full HTML document with an inline layout template: - `<html lang="en">`, `<head>` with meta tags and title, `<body>` with heading, optional date/tags, HTML content, back-link. - Generates an `index.html` with a list of links to all pages. - All user-supplied text is HTML-escaped (XSS prevention). **Frontmatter format** (YAML at the top of each `.md` file): ```yaml --- title: "Page Title" date: "2024-01-01" tags: - tag1 - tag2 --- ``` All three fields are optional -- missing values silently fall back to empty strings/arrays. **Template system**: Currently there is **no template system**. The HTML structure is hardcoded in the `renderLayout`, `renderPage`, and `renderIndex` functions inside `generator.ts`. There are **no separate template files** (no EJS, Handlebars, Nunjucks, etc.). The only customization possible is through modifying the source code directly. --- ### 6. Existing Configuration Files | File | Purpose | |------|---------| | `/tmp/story_3befdab6020a/package.json` | Project manifest, dependencies, scripts, bin entry | | `/tmp/story_3befdab6020a/tsconfig.json` | TypeScript compilation config (target ES2020, CommonJS modules, strict mode, output to `dist/`, includes `src/**/*`, excludes tests) | | `/tmp/story_3befdab6020a/jest.config.js` | Jest config (ts-jest preset, node environment, test pattern `**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts`) | | `/tmp/story_3befdab6020a/.instrument/session.jsonl` | Internal instrumentation log (not project config) | There is **no** `.gitignore`, no `.eslintrc`, no `webpack.config`, and no user-facing configuration file (like `ssg.config.js` or similar) -- the only configuration is via CLI flags `--content` and `--output`. --- ### 7. Template-Related Code Summary The only "template-like" code exists as **inline string templates** in `generator.ts`: - **`renderLayout(title, body)`** (lines 14-26): The "base layout" -- wraps any body content in a minimal HTML5 document. - **`renderPage(page)`** (lines 28-42): The "page template" -- generates the `<h1>`, date, tags, content, and back-link within the body. - **`renderIndex(pages)`** (lines 44-58): The "index template" -- generates the `<h1>Site Index</h1>` heading and `<ul>` of page links. These are all **hardcoded JavaScript functions** producing HTML strings. There are **no configurable templates**, no template engines, no `.html` template files, and no way for users to customize the HTML output without modifying the source code. </task_result> </task>

23:     const raw = fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf-8');
24:     const { data, content } = matter(raw);
25: 
26:     const dateValue = data.date instanceof Date
27:       ? data.date.toISOString().split('T')[0]
28:       : typeof data.date === 'string'
29:         ? data.date
30:         : DEFAULT_FRONTMATTER.date;
31: 
32:     const frontmatter: Frontmatter = {
33:       title: typeof data.title === 'string' ? data.title : DEFAULT_FRONTMATTER.title,
34:       date: dateValue,
35:       tags: Array.isArray(data.tags) ? data.tags : DEFAULT_FRONTMATTER.tags,
36:     };
37: 
38:     const html = marked.parse(content) as string;
39:     const slug = entry.name.replace(/\.md$/, '');
40: 
41:     pages.push({ slug, frontmatter, content, html });
42:   }

44:   pages.sort((a, b) => a.frontmatter.title.localeCompare(b.frontmatter.title));

part.text:
All 41 tests pass, TypeScript compiles cleanly. Here's what was implemented:

**New files:**
- `src/templates.ts` — TemplateEngine class using Handlebars, with built-in defaults and disk-loaded template support
- `templates/layouts/default.hbs` — Default layout template with `{{{body}}}` placeholder
- `templates/page.hbs` — Default page template
- `templates/index.hbs` — Default index template
- `templates/partials/header.hbs`, `footer.hbs`, `nav.hbs` — Reusable partials
- `src/__tests__/templates.test.ts` — 16 template-specific tests

**Modified files:**
- `src/types.ts` — Added optional `template` and `layout` fields to `Frontmatter`
- `src/generator.ts` — Uses `TemplateEngine` instead of hardcoded HTML; accepts optional `templatesDir` parameter
- `src/cli.ts` — Added `--templates <dir>` flag (defaults to `./templates`)
- `src/index.ts` — Exports `TemplateEngine`

**Key behaviors:**
- Pages can specify `template` and/or `layout` in frontmatter
- Falls back to built-in defaults when no template files exist on disk
- Partials loaded from `templates/partials/` are registered at engine init time
- HTML auto-escaped via Handlebars `{{ }}`, raw HTML via `{{{ }}}`
- All existing functionality preserved
